audioScript:
Woman: Did you have a good time at Jim's birthday party?
Boy: Yes, I did. Look at this picture of the party.
Woman: Wow, it looks fun! Which one's Jim?
Boy: He's the boy wearing the red shorts. He's opening a present.
Woman: Oh yes.

Woman: And who's that naughty boy who is <u>throwing grapes</u>?
Boy: Oh, that's <u>David</u>. He's always naughty at school as well.
Woman: Oh dear.

Woman: And which one is Jim's mum? Is she the woman with the short brown hair?
Boy: No, Jim's mum has <u>long blonde curly hair</u>. She's wearing the <u>striped sweater</u>.
Woman: Oh yes, I see her. She doesn't look very happy.
Boy: No! She was angry with David!
Woman: I can't remember her name ...
Boy: She's called <u>Sally</u>.
Woman: Oh yes.

Boy: Can you see <u>Paul</u>?
Woman: Which one's he?
Boy: He's the one who's <u>eating the chocolate cake</u>.
Woman: Is he wearing a <u>spotted green and black T-shirt</u>?
Boy: Yes, that's him. He's smiling here, but he didn't have a very good afternoon.
Woman: Oh dear, why's that?
Boy: Well, he ate too much cake and felt ill.
Woman: Poor Paul.

Boy: And there's <u>Emma</u>. She's in my class at school.
Woman: Is Emma the girl with the guitar?
Boy: No, she's the girl who's <u>playing the drums</u>.
Woman: Was it a noisy party?
Boy: Yes!

Woman: And who's the girl with the guitar then?
Boy: That's <u>Betty</u>.
Woman: Can she play well?
Boy: Yes, very well. We danced to the music later.
Woman: That sounds fun!

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: Listen and write. There is one example.
audioScript:
Girl: What are we doing in our lesson today, Mr Black?
Man: Well, Jane, I'm going to tell you about an interesting new museum that has opened in town. Write down what I say, then you can tell your parents about it.
Girl: OK. What's the name of the museum?
Man: It's called the Station Museum.

Girl: What's inside the museum?
Man: Can you guess?
Girl: Hmm, Station Museum ... is it a train museum?
Man: Yes, well done, Jane. It's full of old <u>trains</u>. Some of them are more than 200 years old.
Girl: Wow! Can we go inside the old trains?
Man: Yes, you can.

Girl: When is it open, Mr Black?
Man: It's open from Tuesday to <u>Saturday</u>.
Girl: So, is it closed on Sunday and Monday?
Man: Yes, that's right.

Girl: And what time does it open?
Man: It opens at nine thirty and it closes at five thirty. Sorry, I mean <u>five fifteen</u>. Yes, that's right, it closes at five fifteen every day.
Girl: OK, I've written that down.

Man: Shall I tell you the address?
Girl: Yes, OK.
Man: It's 16 <u>Digby</u> Road. That's D-I-G-B-Y.
Girl: OK, I've got it.

Girl: Can you tell me the telephone number too?
Man: Yes, of course. It's <u>four three six double two seven</u>.
Girl: Thank you.
Man: That's OK. Perhaps your parents will take you.
Girl: I hope so. Or perhaps we could go on a class visit.
Man: Good idea, Jane.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
William wants to buy some presents for his family. What is he going to buy each person?
Listen and write a letter in each box. There is one example.
audioScript:
Boy: Mum, I want to buy some presents for the family.
Woman: That's very kind, William. What are you going to get everyone?
Boy: Well, Grandma loves chocolate, doesn't she?
Woman: Yes, she does.
Boy: So, I think I'll get her a nice big box of <u>chocolates</u>.
Woman: OK.

Woman: What about Dad? What are you going to get him?
Boy: Hmm, Dad loves taking photos with his camera.
Woman: Yes, you're right.
Boy: So I'm going to get him a <u>book for photographers</u> to help him take even better photos.
Woman: That's a great idea. He'll love that!

Boy: Now, what shall I get for Aunt Pat?
Woman: How about getting her something to wear?
Boy: OK, I'll get her something for the winter. She's got a scarf so I'll get her some wool <u>gloves</u> to keep her warm.
Woman: Excellent.

Boy: Now, what can I get for Uncle Robert?
Woman: He likes playing golf.
Boy: Yes! And he's always losing balls. Shall I get him some <u>golf balls</u>?
Woman: Yes, I think that's a good idea.

Woman: And don't forget your cousins! What are you going to get for Sarah?
Boy: Well, she likes colouring pictures. Shall I get her a box of pencils in lots of different colours? Maybe I could get her a <u>book of pictures to colour</u> too?
Woman: I think that she'll be very happy with that.
Boy: Great!

Boy: Now, what about Katy? That's more difficult. What does she like doing?
Woman: She likes writing her diary. You could get her a pen?
Boy: No, I don't want to buy a pen. I want to buy her a <u>diary</u> for next year.
Woman: Oh yes, that's a very good idea! Now, what are you going to get me?
Boy: I'm not going to tell you! You'll have to wait and see.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: Listen and tick (✓) the box. There is one example.

example.question: Which holiday did Michael have this year?

items.question: How did Michael go on holiday?
Where did Michael stay?
options: under some trees next to a river

items.question: What did Michael do on holiday?
What did Michael eat on holiday?
What time did Michael go to sleep on holiday?

audioScript:
Woman: Hi, Michael. Did you have a good holiday?
Boy: Yes, I did.
Woman: Did you go to the beach?
Boy: No, I wanted to ski in the mountains, but it was too expensive. So we <u>camped in a tent</u> this year.

Woman: That sounds like fun.
Boy: Yes, it was.
Woman: How did you get there? Did you go by train?
Boy: No, we wanted to take our bikes with us so we went <u>by car</u>.

Woman: And where did you camp? Did you put your tent on the beach?
Boy: No, we found a nice field where we wanted to put our tent. But the farmer said we couldn't camp there. So then we found a better place <u>under some trees and next to a river</u>.
Woman: That sounds lovely!

Woman: And what did you do on holiday? Did you go swimming in the river?
Boy: No, it was too cold. Dad did do some fishing in the river.
Woman: Did you do some fishing?
Boy: No, I <u>played football</u> with my brothers every day.

Woman: And what did you eat? Did you get your favourite burgers and chips?
Boy: No, no burgers! We ate the <u>fish</u> that Dad got when he fished in the river.
Woman: Hmm, talking about it is making me hungry!
Boy: The fish was very good!

Woman: Did you go to bed very late each night?
Boy: Yes, I usually go to bed at seven thirty or eight o'clock, but I didn't go to sleep on holiday until it was dark. That was <u>nine thirty</u>!
Woman: That's very late!
Boy: Yes, it was fun!

items.item: The man's scarf (the man who is skiing)
The smaller boy's trousers (in front of the snowman)

audioScript:
Girl: This picture looks interesting.
Man: Would you like to colour it?
Girl: Yes, please.
Man: OK. Can you see the car next to the house?
Girl: Yes, I can.
Man: Good. Colour it <u>green</u>.
Girl: OK.

Girl: What else shall I colour?
Man: Can you see the man who is skiing?
Girl: Yes, I can. That looks fun.
Man: Can you colour his scarf <u>blue</u>?
Girl: OK.

Girl: What shall I colour now?
Man: Let's see. There are two boys who are making a snowman?
Girl: Yes, I can see them. That's a great snowman!
Man: Can you see the smaller boy? He's in front of the snowman.
Girl: Yes, I can.
Man: Colour his trousers <u>purple</u>.
Girl: OK.

Girl: Can I write something in the picture now?
Man: Yes, good idea.
Girl: What shall I write?
Man: Can you write the word "<u>hat</u>" on the snowman's head?
Girl: Yes, of course! He looks like he wants to wear a hat!
Man: Yes, he does!

Man: Would you like to write something else now?
Girl: Yes!
Man: OK. Can you see the house at the back of the picture?
Girl: Yes, I can.
Man: Well, that's not a house. It's a café. Can you write the word "<u>café</u>" on it?
Girl: OK, I'll do that now.

Man: Now for some more colouring.
Girl: Oh, good.
Man: Can you see the girl with a big ball made of snow?
Girl: Yes, I can.
Man: Can you colour that ball <u>yellow</u>?
Girl: OK. The picture looks more interesting now, doesn't it?
Man: Yes, it does.
